Round 1 Planning: I will use my team (owner_2) to exploit the price curve. Strategy: (1) Charge 10 MWh in Block 1 (night, base 20) to store energy. (2) Hold in Block 2 (morning, base 50). (3) Discharge 10 MWh in Block 3 (peak, base 90). (4) Hold in Block 4 (evening, base 60). This captures the high peak prices while "purchasing" cheap energy during night.

Note: Final game length is uncertain (prob 0.75 survives each day). We must act now.

ROUND 1 PLANNING - BLOCK 1 OF 4 (NIGHT, BASE 20)

My strategy: partner with owner_1 (team owner_1 + owner_2).

Block 1 (night): HOLD. Let owner_1 charge 10 MWh at the high realized price (base 20 +2*(10)) = 40. I pay nothing, maximize owner_1's opportunity.

Block 2 (morning, base 50): HOLD. No action needed.

Block 3 (peak, base 90): owner_1 DISCHARGE 10 MWh. Realized price = 90 - 2*(10 from discharge) = 70. Revenue ~700. I hold.

Block 4 (evening, base 60): HOLD. No action needed.

Team total profit = owner_1's cost (400 in block 1) + owner_1's revenue (700 in block 3) - owner_2's cost (0) = 300 credits across the day.

Key insight: I avoid paying for charging in block 1, letting owner_1 capture the night price premium.

As owner_3, I will hold in Block 1 (night). Strategy: wait for Block 2 (day 2) night. If no other owners charge, I will charge 10 MWh at night, hold morning, discharge 10 MWh at peak, hold evening — capturing the 300-credit profit cycle. I will not interfere with owner_1's planned night charge/discharge so as not to raise the night realized price and erode the peak price.

End of planning for block 1. Ready for block 2 results.
Plan: Hold in block 2. Expected to survive to day 2 night, then charge 10 MWh, hold morning, discharge 10 MWh at peak, hold evening.
Now in block 2 (morning, base 50). All previous owners announced: owner_1, owner_2, owner_3, owner_4 all held. No one is charging or discharging.

In block 2, I have 0 stored. With no one charging or discharging, the realized price for my block will be the base price of 50 (no balance in transit). If I charge now, I'd pay the full 50 (charging cost). Better to hold and not incur a cost.

As owner_4, I will hold in Block 2 (morning). With all other owners holding and no balance in transit, the realized price is base 50. Charging would raise the realized price to 70, making it unprofitable. Holding preserves battery capacity for future blocks.

For Day 2 (next grid day), the night block has base 20. I will charge 10 MWh in the night block. This is the same strategy owner_1 (and owner_2) planned for Block 1 night: buy cheap, store energy, discharge at peak (block 3) at the high realized price. This should yield ~300 credits profit per day if the game continues.

On Day 2 (grid day 2, Block 1 night), owner_1 already charged 10 MWh last night (block 1 of day 1). Since owner_1 will discharge 10 MWh in Block 3 (peak, base 90) this same day, the net effect is that owner_1's battery will be depleted by Block 3. The game will then continue to Day 2 with owner_1 potentially empty (or partially charged). As owner_4, I will charge 10 MWh in the night block of Day 2 and wait for the peak block. I will hold in the morning and evening blocks unless another owner charges/discharges, in which case I will follow suit.

Round 3 — Block 3 (peak) results: realized price is 90 credits (no net balance in transit). All held. Battery still 0/10. Now moving to Block 4 (evening, base 60). Strategy: if game survives to Day 2, plan to charge in Day 2 night and discharge in Day 2 peak. If game ends, no further action needed.

I will hold this block. With owner_1 discharging 10 MWh, the realized price for any charging would be 40+2x per MWh, which is unprofitable.
